aliases: KEK to Kamioka long-baseline neutrino oscillation experiment

facility_roles.note: K2K used the existing Super-Kamiokande detector, owned by the separate Super-Kamiokande experiment/collaboration, as its far detector.
facility_roles.quote: the neutrino beam enters the earth and emerges at Super-Kamiokande, 250 km away.

intervals.label: beam line and detector preparation
intervals.note: No construction-start date was found; the March-1998 conference paper describes the experiment as 'in preparation'.
intervals.quote: A long-baseline neutrino-oscillation experiment using a well-defined neutrino beam is in preparation at KEK.

intervals.label: beam commissioning
intervals.note: The KEK tutorial page (written before the event) says commissioning 'is scheduled' for January 1999; physics data taking began in June 1999 per the measurement paper. No source confirms the actual commissioning month.
intervals.quote: The commissioning of the neutrino beam is scheduled in January, 1999.

intervals.label: data taking ended
intervals.note: K2K data taking ended in November 2004; the KEK-PS itself continued operating other experiments until December 2005.

name: K2K (KEK to Kamioka)
notes: T2K's own lineage record (experiment:t2k) lists K2K as its predecessor; per this workstream's instructions lineage is authored once, on the later entity.
Derived fields (detector_ids, site_ids, result_ids, document_ids) are deliberately not written (v0.2 A1).
No near-detector records are created for K2K in this workstream: the task brief requested only experiment:k2k and collaboration:k2k.

physics_goals.quote: the KEK neutrino beam is directed through the earth to Super-Kamiokande, providing a controlled “laboratory” source of neutrinos, allowing us to check Super-K results obtained from atmospheric neutrinos
physics_goals.value: Use a well-understood, controlled accelerator neutrino beam to check the atmospheric-neutrino oscillation interpretation from Super-Kamiokande

physics_goals.quote: explore the neutrino mass difference-squared Dm2~10-2 eV^2 region
physics_goals.value: Measure muon-neutrino disappearance to probe the neutrino mass-squared difference around Delta m^2 ~ 1e-2 eV^2

summary.plain: The world's first long-baseline neutrino experiment: a beam of neutrinos made at KEK's proton accelerator was sent 250 km through the Earth to the Super-Kamiokande detector, to check whether the atmospheric neutrino puzzle Super-K had already seen was really neutrino oscillation.
summary.technical: Accelerator neutrino oscillation experiment: 12 GeV protons from KEK-PS on an aluminium target, decay-pipe muon-neutrino beam (mean energy ~1.5 GeV) monitored by a near detector complex at KEK, observed 250 km away at Super-Kamiokande. Ran June 1999 - November 2004; reported muon-neutrino disappearance consistent with oscillation at 4.3 sigma (Phys. Rev. D 74, 072003, 2006). Direct predecessor of T2K.
